name: two_shooters
description: Eleven frames of one kiss from two bodies, three hundred milliseconds out of step.
why: Section 10.1's 'two cameras shooting the same kiss produce one moment with two sub-groups'. It is one moment because it is one kiss - a photographer delivering this would never call the second shooter's angle a separate event - and two bursts because a burst is a fact about one shutter and neither body knows what the other did. Both halves matter: one moment with one burst would have lost the per-camera structure phase 26 needs, and two moments would have double-counted the kiss in phase 12's coverage.
labelled_by: PHASE-08 section 8 step 9, authored ground truth
